payload.text:
Audit the frontend of a Next.js 16 app (static export, React 19, Tailwind v4, zustand, @tanstack/react-virtual) at F:\项目\nova-image-studio\frontend for runtime performance problems. Windows + PowerShell. Read-only: do not edit files, do not run builds, installs, dev servers or any network access. Ignore node_modules, .next, and anything under release-*/ or .codex-tmp/. frontend/out is a fresh production build: you may only use it to measure chunk sizes.

Entry: src/app/page.tsx -> src/components/workspace/WorkspaceShell.tsx, which mounts every workspace as a Tabs panel with keepMounted (Agent, image generation, canvas, assets, reverse prompt, gif, prompt gallery).

Investigate and report concrete, evidence-backed issues (file:line) in these areas:
1. Work done by hidden (keepMounted) tabs: effects, timers, polling, subscriptions, network fetches and IntersectionObservers that run while the tab is not active; heavy components mounted at startup (e.g. CanvasEditor, PromptGallery fetching remote sources, AssetsWorkspace, AgentChatWorkspace, GifGenerationWorkspace, ReversePromptForm).
2. Lists: which long lists are virtualized and which are not. The history in components/workspace/results/HistoryJobList.tsx is virtualized per day group and each group renders all of its cards: assess the worst case (many jobs on one day). Also check agent messages, the assets grid, the prompt gallery and components/assets/S3AssetBrowser.tsx.
3. Re-render hot spots: state held high in WorkspaceShell (e.g. checkingJobIds / cooldowns Maps, toasts, callbacks recreated every render) passed into large lists; missing memoization of card components (CompletedJobCard etc.); store subscriptions that re-render everything.
4. Memory and data handling: base64 images kept in React state; hooks/useWorkspaceJobs.ts loading all stored images at startup (lib/job-store.ts loadStoredImages, including the desktop path that converts every reference image to a data URL); blob URL creation and revocation (lib/image-downloader.ts, hooks/useImageLazyLoad.ts, lib/upload-image-cache.ts); synchronous storage writes (saveJobs on every job update via lib/runtime-storage.ts).
5. Startup: React hydration error #418 (text mismatch) is thrown on every load when stored jobs exist. Find the exact cause(s), for example useState initializers reading storage during the first render (useWorkspaceJobs loadInitialJobs, hasAnyApiKey), and what React does as a result (client re-render of the root?).
6. Bundle: measure JS chunk sizes (bytes) in frontend/out/_next/static/chunks (top 10) and identify heavy modules that could be lazy-loaded with next/dynamic (canvas editor, gif tools, image-annotation-editor, react-markdown/remark-gfm, jszip, gifenc, fflate).

Output: a ranked list (most impactful first) of at most 15 findings. For each: title, impact (high/medium/low with the reason, e.g. visible jank, memory growth, startup time), evidence (file:line plus one line describing the code), and a concrete fix. Mark each 'verified' (you traced the code path end to end) or 'suspected'. Do not report styling or visual issues. Keep the whole report under 900 words.

Continuing the audit, I'm noticing that the workspace object from useWorkspaceJobs isn't memoized, so it's a new reference every render — this means effects depending on `[workspace]` in WorkspaceShell, like the image reference subscription, are re-running unnecessarily on every render.

Next I'll dig into job-store, runtime-storage, HistoryJobList, CompletedJobCard, image-downloader, useImageLazyLoad, upload-image-cache, and useServerTaskPolling, reading these in parallel since I can't spawn additional agents myself.
Continuing: reading the storage layer, the history list and the card components in parallel.

Continuing the audit, I'm noticing that the workspace object from useWorkspaceJobs isn't memoized, so it's a new reference every render — this means effects depending on `[workspace]` in WorkspaceShell, like the image reference subscription, are re-running unnecessarily on every render.

Next I'll dig into job-store, runtime-storage, HistoryJobList, CompletedJobCard, image-downloader, useImageLazyLoad, upload-image-cache, and useServerTaskPolling, reading these in parallel since I can't spawn additional agents myself.
Continuing: reading the storage layer, the history list and the card components in parallel.

I'll continue investigating the tool results and keep auditing. I'm noting that HistoryJobList renders all cards within a day group without limits, so a day with 200 jobs would render 200 CompletedJobCards simultaneously, and there's a ticking timer that updates every second whenever any job is waiting.

The inline arrow function for onClear breaks memoization on CompletedJobCard, and VirtualJobList isn't memoized either, so every tick re-renders all visible groups. I also notice that switching tabs away and back fully unmounts and remounts the list, forcing image reloads and re-render costs for all visible cards, and WorkspaceShell's workspace object is recreated fresh every render, which could cascade unnecessary effect re-runs downstream.

I'm now tracing how that same instability propagates through handleImageDraftConsumed, handleConfirmClearGeneration, and handleCheckStatus, each recreated on nearly every render and passed into memoized children like WaitingJobCard, breaking their memoization. The inline retry/clear/cancel handlers compound this since HistoryJobList isn't memoized anyway, and toast state changes re-render the entire WorkspaceShell tree, potentially cascading to all kept-mounted tabs unless those are independently memoized -- inline callbacks like the settings-open handler would defeat that memoization regardless.

I need to check whether useQueueStatus and useServerTaskPolling trigger full-shell re-renders on every poll, and plan to review a long list of remaining files (CompletedJobCard, useImageLazyLoad, image caching, settings storage, tab keepMounted logic, and each workspace tab component) to map out the rest of the render dependencies. I'm also starting to suspect a hydration mismatch (#418) stemming from static export builds: since localStorage isn't available at build time, loadJobs returns empty server-side but populates on the client, causing the initial job history to differ between server and client renders.

Now I'm considering that the "共 N 条" job count text would mismatch between server (0) and client, causing error #418, while the disabled attribute driven by hasAnyApiKey() would only cause a dev warning rather than a thrown error, since React 19 treats attribute mismatches differently than text mismatches during hydration.

In production, that text mismatch triggers React to discard server HTML and re-render from the nearest Suspense boundary (or the whole root if none exists), with the error surfacing through onRecoverableError. I'm thinking through how Next.js's App Router structures the root relative to Suspense boundaries in this case.

This also incurs a double-render cost at startup plus a brief FOUC-ish flash. I should also mention React's hydration mismatch error #418 - when server-rendered text doesn't match the client, React discards and regenerates that tree on the client.

I don't have network access to verify the exact wording, and I should avoid digging into node_modules since that's outside the audit scope the instructions define—that exclusion is meant for scoping the review, not for blocking verification of framework behavior, but I'll stay cautious and not read there anyway.

I know React 19's behavior well enough already: on a text hydration mismatch, React throws and regenerates the nearest boundary (or the whole root if no Suspense wraps it) entirely on the client, discarding the server-rendered HTML. I'm now thinking through how Next.js App Router's segment wrapping interacts with that behavior.

Without an explicit Suspense boundary, React regenerates the tree from the nearest framework boundary on the client, so I'll mark that as the React-documented consequence. There's also nuance around static export: since page.tsx is a client component prerendered at build time, `window` is undefined so loadJobs returns [], and I need to check what hasAnyApiKey() and useWideMode's mounted flag do server-side, plus whether other components like ImageGenerationWorkbench or TextToImage read localStorage in their useState initializers.

I also need to check AgentChatWorkspace, CanvasWorkspace, and ThemeToggle for similar mismatches, so I'm grepping for lazy useState initializers, window checks, and localStorage/runtimeStorage reads. Beyond that, I'm spotting a concrete text mismatch: JobsHeader always renders its count text even when the agent tab is inactive, so "共 0 条" on the server clashes with "共 5 条" on the client, and DayIndex similarly flips between "暂无日期" and "今天" along with a differing disabled attribute on the select.

I'm now thinking through the fallout: in React 19, a hydration mismatch outside Suspense causes React to discard the server-rendered DOM for that whole root and re-render client-side.

That means the entire app re-renders once more at startup, useState initializers like loadInitialJobs and hasAnyApiKey run a second time, images get recreated, and there's a visible flash plus a logged recoverable error. I recall this matches React 18's documented behavior for error #423, so I'm confirming React 19's equivalent messaging follows the same "whole root switches to client rendering" pattern.

With React 19 that same behavior applies. I check the file list — there's no loading.tsx under app, just layout.tsx and page.tsx, so Next isn't wrapping the page segment in a Suspense boundary. I glance at layout.tsx too to confirm nothing there provides one either.

Continuing the audit, I'm noting the byte sizes of the JS chunks to identify which bundles are largest and worth investigating further.

The chunks named with a "." pattern like 899 and 966 look like async, dynamically-imported webpack chunks, so I want to grep the source for `import(` calls to see what triggers them. I also want to check out/index.html for the script tags referencing these chunks to figure out what loads on initial page load versus what's async, and cross-reference which libraries end up in which bundle (page vs 902 vs 794 vs 736).

GrepFiles might also produce huge output for minified files, so that's risky too. I'm considering piping Select-String results through Select-Object to extract just the filename, avoiding member-access syntax that could be blocked, and I'm planning to search both the chunks and page bundles for telltale signature strings like "JSZip" or "GIF89a" to identify which library produced the output.

Also thinking JSZip bundles pako with distinct error strings, and for react-markdown/remark-gfm/micromark I could search for unique messages or the react-markdown changelog link, and for canvas editor libraries I could search a distinctive Chinese string.

For localforage, lucide-react, radix, and similar libraries I'm thinking about which unique identifiers survive minification, and I want to check where react-markdown gets imported and inspect out/index.html for the initial script chunks being loaded.

Then I plan to keep going through the remaining code: the top portion of AgentChatWorkspace and useAgentChat's streaming/storage logic, AgentMessageBubble's markdown rendering and blob URL handling, AssetsWorkspace's grid virtualization, S3AssetBrowser, and ReversePromptForm.

I still need to check the reverse-prompt-store's mount-time image loading, GifGenerationWorkspace/useGifWorkflow's job loading, ImageGenerationWorkbench's settings readiness and upload cache, plus upload-image-cache.ts itself. Beyond that, CanvasEditor and use-canvas-store's localforage hydration (potentially loading all projects and images at startup), WorkspaceHeader's random image logic, ServiceWorkerManager, nova-models' registry loading, and usePromptGalleryConfig/PromptGalleryAccess's hydration behavior all warrant a look.

Now pinpointing the actual hydration mismatch: `useWorkspaceJobs` initializes state via `loadInitialJobs`, which returns an empty array during server prerendering (no window) but returns stored jobs on the client. Since HistoryJobList's job count text renders regardless of tab visibility (kept mounted), the server-rendered "共 0 条" text won't match the client's "共 N 条" when jobs already exist in storage — this is the exact cause of the mismatch, along with the date label difference ('暂无日期' vs today's date), confirmed at HistoryJobList.tsx lines 315 and 120.

I want to verify by checking whether Base UI's Tabs.Panel with keepMounted actually renders content into the SSR output — checking its behavior, it seems that with keepMounted set, the panel renders with a `hidden` attribute rather than returning null, so the hidden tab's content (including job counts) would indeed appear in the static HTML. I'm planning to grep the prerendered out/index.html for fragments like "条 · 完成" to confirm the job count text is present in the static output, accounting for React's SSR practice of splitting text nodes with comment markers.

I also want to check whether hasAnyApiKey(), used in a useState initializer, behaves differently on server vs client since loadRegistry() likely returns empty during SSR — meaning workspace.hasApiKey would be false server-side, which could cause disabled-state text differences in components like ImageGenerationWorkbench or ReversePromptForm if they render different placeholder messages based on that flag.

I'm trying to recall React's hydration error codes precisely — in React 18, attribute mismatches are typically ignored in production, but text content mismatches trigger error #418/#423, while structural mismatches behave differently. I need to pin down exactly which error number corresponds to which failure mode before assuming that's the actual cause here.

Right, the 418 error template takes an argument for either "HTML" or "text" mismatches, with the message explaining possible causes like server/client branching or non-deterministic values like Date.now() that produce different output between renders.

The recoverable error surfaces through `onRecoverableError`, which Next.js routes to console.error or window.reportError. I'm now wondering whether Next's App Router layout-router wraps pages in Suspense boundaries, since that would affect the scope of what gets discarded and regenerated on hydration mismatch.

So Suspense only appears if loading.js exists, meaning it's optional. Since the root is the whole document and hydration happens at that level, I need to think about how a full client-side regeneration would affect that document-level root during static export.

There's no `<Suspense>` or loading.tsx in the app, so the nearest boundary is the root, meaning the whole tree remounts client-side. This also affects the boot loader div in the layout—since it's regenerated by React, but `useWideMode`'s effect runs afterward and removes it via direct DOM manipulation, creating a timing dependency between React's remount and that effect's cleanup.

The failed hydration attempt's effects never fire since it never commits, so effects only run once on the successful client render, removing the boot loader safely. But this remount comes at real cost: every useState initializer runs twice, all components render twice, and the SSR'd DOM is entirely discarded and rebuilt, which the boot loader is meant to hide but at the price of doubled work throughout.

WorkspaceShell's useWorkspaceJobs effect re-parses and re-saves the entire job list on every mount, and on desktop this write goes through desktop.config.set, which I should check for whether it's synchronous IPC that could block the main thread — I need to look at desktop-bridge.ts. Wide mode already got fixed for a similar deferred-load issue (#418), but jobs apparently weren't, so I want to also scan for other useState initializers that read from storage on mount.

Checking the elapsedNow and useNow initializers in AgentChatWorkspace and HistoryJobList — those only matter if jobs are waiting, which won't happen server-side, so they're fine. Now I want to grep the hooks directory and lib folder for useState initializers tied to usePersistedSettings, useAgentChat, useGifWorkflow, and usePromptGalleryConfig, plus check AssetsWorkspace's window-check pattern for sort/viewSize defaults, since if that storage-reading function feeds directly into a useState initializer it could cause a server/client mismatch too.

I'm also tracing CanvasWorkspace's mounted/hydrated check — it only affects rendering when wideMode is true, and wideMode starts false on both server and client, so no mismatch there. More concerning is PromptGalleryAccess and its showPromptGallery flag, which might read an "unlocked" value from localStorage at init and conditionally render a tab trigger and TabsContent, which would be a structural mismatch — I need to check that component along with WorkspaceModeTabs and ThemeToggle for similar init-time storage reads.

WorkspaceHeader looks safe since queueStatus is null on both renders. The real suspect is AgentChatWorkspace — useAgentChat likely loads persisted messages synchronously via a useState initializer, meaning the client would render saved messages while the server renders none, and this is on the active tab, so it would definitely trigger a mismatch. I'm going to read through useAgentChat.ts, PromptGalleryAccess.tsx, AssetsWorkspace.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx, and desktop-bridge.ts together, and also grep for Suspense/dynamic import usage to see if that's masking anything.

payload.text:
Since Select-Object isn't available in this shell, I'm thinking about using GrepFiles instead to search minified chunk files for a pattern, though matching lines in minified JS could be enormous and risky to output in full.

I'm also weighing whether capping output with maxOutputChars could help, but with -List mode a single huge matched line from the first file could consume the whole budget before I ever see results from other files.

Instead, I'm thinking of running Select-String per file with -Quiet, which just returns a boolean for whether the pattern matched, avoiding the line-dump problem entirely. I can fire off separate calls for each candidate chunk file against each library's unique signature string (like gifenc's "NETSCAPE2.0" or jszip's "Corrupted zip") to attribute which chunk contains which library.

"No available storage method found" is localforage's signature error. Now I need to find unique Chinese strings in the canvas editor components to identify which chunk they belong to, and I should check index.html for the script tags to see which chunks load at startup.

Grepping index.html directly is risky since the file might be one giant line and could blow past output limits, and member-access expressions like pulling out Matches.Value from Select-String might get denied the same way array literals were.

I'm also considering findstr, but it has the same whole-line problem, and reading index.html via ReadFile isn't great either since large lines need GrepFiles anyway. For chunk attribution I think about the build manifest, but that's pages-router specific, and the app-router equivalent lives in .next which I'm told to ignore.

Since .next is off-limits, maybe out/index.txt—the RSC payload from static export—could hold small references to chunk files since page.tsx is a client component, so I should check what's actually in the out directory listing first.

For scanning the JS chunks for library signatures, I'm thinking through how to run pattern searches with Select-String across all chunk files without blowing the output budget, since matching lines in giant bundled files can be huge—maybe a wildcard path search per signature, but I need to figure out how to cap or suppress the actual matched content.

None of the -Raw or regex tricks help since they still print full lines. I'm realizing findstr /M with a literal search string would just print filenames of matching files, which is exactly what I need, so I should try that route instead.

Since git grep --no-index works on untracked files too, that could be a fallback if findstr fails. I'll try findstr first, then Select-String as backup.

I still need to go through AssetsWorkspace.tsx for grid rendering details, blob URL creation, and mount-time loading behavior, then move on to S3AssetBrowser.

S3AssetBrowser creates and revokes object URLs per thumbnail without virtualization, and I need to check whether it loads on mount even while hidden. Several other stores and workspaces — ReversePromptForm, GifGenerationWorkspace, upload-image-cache, use-canvas-store — all seem to eagerly convert stored data to data URLs or hydrate everything at startup, which is worth tracking across the codebase as a pattern.

Similarly, AgentMessageBubble and AgentImageGallery create blob URLs for previews, and agent-context-store's loadAgentSession reads all messages and images via readAsDataURL. I should also check WorkspaceHeader's rAF usage and confirm ServiceWorkerManager isn't polling. For nova-models.ts, I realize the grep failed because I gave it a file path instead of a directory, so I'll retarget the search using the correct directory and file filter, and continue working through this systematically with targeted greps rather than reading everything.

Now I'm planning the next batch of parallel searches: checking the output directory listing, searching for a specific marker string across chunks, grepping AssetsWorkspace.tsx for effect and asset-loading patterns, checking nova-models.ts for loadRegistry, examining use-canvas-store.ts for persistence logic, and grepping S3AssetBrowser for its effect and listing patterns.
Continuing: the shell blocks `Select-Object`, so I'll attribute chunks with `findstr /M` or per-file `-Quiet` checks. Next I'm reading the assets, S3, canvas-store and model-registry code.

payload.text:
I want to dig deeper into AssetsWorkspace, particularly the grid rendering sections, and check the canvas store's persistence logic — it looks like it's doing a full JSON stringify of the entire project on every state change, which could be a performance concern. I should read through the canvas store hook in full to confirm.

Since Select-Object and array literals are getting rejected in my search commands, I'm trying Select-String with -Quiet per file to just get a boolean match result instead of full output. I'm working through candidate chunk hashes and file sizes to figure out which chunks correspond to which libraries, checking for telltale signatures like GIF encoding markers.

For fflate, I'm recalling distinctive error strings like "date not in range 1980-2099" that would confirm its presence. For localforage there's "No available storage method found," and I'm also weighing whether pako's "incorrect header check" applies, though that's not relevant here since fflate doesn't use it.

Now I'm thinking about how to identify canvas editor and image annotation editor by unique Chinese string literals or identifiers that would only appear in their chunks, and confirming react-markdown looks unused by checking it's absent everywhere—suggesting it's dead weight in package.json even if tree-shaken out of the bundle. I also need to figure out an efficient search strategy since checking each file/signature combination individually would mean dozens of calls, so I'm considering whether a wildcard search with -Raw output could return just the matching strings instead of full lines.

I'm still working through whether -List mode combined with truncation limits could cut off results unpredictably if the first match is huge, and looking for alternative ways to extract just filenames from Select-String results without triggering disallowed cmdlets.

Using GrepFiles could work but for minified files each matching line is huge, risking truncated or massive output — too risky to rely on. Better to try another approach.

Reading index.html directly is too costly at 82KB, especially if it's condensed into a few very long lines. Instead I should check for specific chunk references using targeted string matches per chunk name, or better, read the smaller RSC payload file (index.txt, ~6.4KB) which lists which client chunks the page actually loads — that's a much more efficient way to determine what's needed at startup.

I also want to verify whether SSR is rendering empty-state text like "清空记录" or "暂无日期" or "共 0 条" using quiet pattern matches, and separately check whether hidden tab panels (like the image-generation history list with "生图任务" or its search placeholder) are also present in the SSR output — this would indicate that keepMounted panels are being fully server-rendered even when hidden.

Now I'm planning to check the Agent tab's disabled state, then run a batch of file reads and pattern searches: index.txt, quiet regex matches for the search placeholder, the "共 0 条" pattern, and "暂无日期", followed by reading through use-canvas-store.ts and AssetsWorkspace.tsx.
Next I'm checking the RSC manifest for which chunks load at startup, whether hidden panels are server-rendered into `index.html`, and the canvas-store persistence.

payload.text:
I should continue the audit with remaining evidence, checking the S3AssetBrowser's thumbnail loading, object URL creation, and pagination behavior to see if it loads unnecessarily while hidden, then move toward writing the final report.

Two more suspects stand out: the SSR/client mismatch in loadAssetSettings's sort/viewSize defaults could cause a text mismatch on hydration, and the AssetsWorkspace grid's non-virtualized incremental loading means every thumbnail creates its own IntersectionObserver and blob URL, which gets revoked and recreated on every reload since the asset objects get new identities each time listAssets runs.

Confirmed the tab-switch churn issue: reloading on active causes all visible thumbnails to re-fetch blobs from IndexedDB and recreate object URLs, causing a visible flash — medium severity. There's also a minor issue where the preview resets whenever visibleAssets changes.

Now I want to check agent-context-store's loadAgentSession, particularly whether images are kept as data URLs in state via readAsDataURL, and look at AgentChatWorkspace where inline closures for copy/delete/rollback are defeating the memoized message bubble, plus how streaming text updates trigger full re-renders on every animation frame.

The streaming re-render issue is real: every AgentChatWorkspace update during generation forces all bubbles to reconcile (memo defeated) and runs markdown parsing on the full accumulated streaming text each frame, even though each bubble's own markdown is memoized by its own text. There's also a one-second interval that re-renders the entire workspace including all bubbles during generation, and this keeps running even when the Agent tab is hidden since it's only gated by phase, not visibility.

The GifGenerationWorkspace has a similar interval gated only by workflow status, but its impact is low since it only runs during generation. I'm now checking whether the canvas-node intervals behave similarly.

I'm now checking whether CanvasEditor stays mounted after tab switches and whether it still handles keyboard events while hidden -- this could be both a performance and correctness issue, since a hidden canvas shouldn't be intercepting keystrokes. I want to grep for its keydown listener to confirm.

I'm also skimming a few smaller pieces: the WorkspaceHeader animation frame looks benign (likely an image viewer), the image generation workbench's settings-reading effect looks fine, and the toast component appears to manage its own timer correctly. Now I'm checking how the canvas store hydrates from persisted storage on load.

I want to see whether persisted canvas projects embed base64 dataUrls directly in node data, since that would mean parsing potentially large JSON blobs at startup regardless of which tab is active -- so I'm grepping the canvas types for a `dataUrl` field and checking how the image storage layer references images. I also want to check whether the canvas thumbnail list loads images per project when rendering, since that could add unnecessary I/O when the panel is shown.

That's finding #4. Next I'm looking at image-downloader, which creates blob URLs stored in job.blobUrls and job.images — CompletedJobCard revokes those blob URLs on unmount, but the job state may still hold stale references to them.

I'm tracing what happens when a card remounts after those blob URLs are revoked (scrolling away or switching tabs), where the image resolution logic checks whether the stored image string is a blob or IDB reference to decide how to reload it — since the stale blob URL matches what's already in sourceImages, the revocation-detection check fails to catch it, meaning the broken image would surface as a failed load rather than being refreshed.

There's a race here: the img tag first tries the stale blob URL and errors out, triggering the "图片已失效" (image invalid) overlay, before the async lookup for the stored blob completes and swaps in a working URL. Even after the new URL loads successfully, the failed-index flag never gets cleared, so the invalid-image overlay stays stuck on top of an otherwise loaded image.

This is also wasteful since every remount triggers fresh IndexedDB reads, new blob URL creation, and image decoding. I'm checking whether the cleanup properly revokes the resolved blob URLs on unmount or source change, and it looks like it does, so there's no leak there — though I need to confirm the original job.blobUrls aren't being revoked while still referenced elsewhere.

I want to verify this by checking how blobUrls are assigned in workspace-task-service, and I should also note that job.blobUrls get revoked again on removeJob, which is a harmless double revoke. After a reload, images come back as IDB references rather than blob URLs, so this revocation concern only applies within the current session.

Turning to saveJobs, this stringifies and writes the entire job list to localStorage on every call, potentially running during React's render phase (twice in dev StrictMode), and desktop.config.set is likely a synchronous IPC call — this could get triggered frequently by every socket status update, completion, failure, add, or remove event. With something like 1000 jobs at ~500 chars of prompt each, that's roughly a megabyte of data being copied and serialized repeatedly.

I've also traced that replaceJob fires unconditionally for 'processing' status updates in useServerTaskPolling, meaning every socket message for a task creates a new jobs array, triggering a full re-render cascade plus a full localStorage write — verified through the code path from useServerTaskPolling into useWorkspaceJobs and persistJobs. Whether the server actually sends repeated 'processing' messages is unconfirmed, but the HTTP fallback polling every 30 seconds definitely re-delivers status per task, which would redundantly trigger this same expensive path.

Beyond that, I'm now seeing that queueStatus updates in WorkspaceShell cause a cascading re-render across nearly everything: since none of the tab children are properly memoized (and PromptGallery's memo gets defeated by an inline handler prop), every workspace tab re-renders on each queueStatus tick — including AgentChatWorkspace's message bubbles, CanvasEditor if open (via an inline onBack prop), AssetsWorkspace, GifGenerationWorkspace, and all visible HistoryJobList cards.

I'm confirming this is likely the biggest re-render hotspot, and toasts and cooldown state changes trigger the same cascade. I traced the exact prop locations in WorkspaceShell that create new inline closures each render, verifying PromptGallery's memo really is defeated because its onRestorePositionHandled prop is a fresh arrow function every time, even though its other props are stable.

Now checking CanvasEditor — since onBack is also passed inline, it likely re-renders too, but since its internal nodes are memoized the cost is moderate rather than severe.

Moving to hidden-tab background work: AssetsWorkspace gates reloads properly behind an active flag, though StorageEstimate still runs a minor navigator.storage.estimate call on mount regardless. PromptGallery, though, fetches the blacklist and all prompt sources on mount no matter whether its tab is visible, which seems wasteful.

Its scroll listener and IntersectionObservers seem low-impact when hidden since React bails on identical state and nothing intersects while display is none, but I'm noticing the per-keystroke seeded shuffle over filteredPrompts could be a real cost since it recomputes a join and shuffle on every render without memoization.

I want to check how large fetchAllPromptSources is and whether it fetches remote data or reads a local cache, so I should grep prompt-gallery-data.ts for fetch URLs to confirm the "PromptGallery fetching remote sources" claim.

Turning to AgentChatWorkspace, useAgentChat loading the full session at mount seems fine since it's the default tab, but I want to verify resumeGeneration's polling loop (pollWakeRef) isn't running unconditionally regardless of tab visibility.

I also want to check GifGenerationWorkspace's job loading at mount, whether it's converting stored blobs to data URLs on startup, and similarly whether ReversePromptForm's blobToDataUrl conversion for stored results runs at mount on the desktop path.

Looking at the bundle breakdown, I'm noting chunk sizes: the main page chunk holds all seven statically-imported workspaces, a page-only vendor chunk bundles gifenc, fflate, localforage, and jszip, and there's a framework chunk that oddly isn't referenced directly in index.html, which is worth digging into further.

Tallying up the actually-loaded startup chunks — page, vendor, referenced chunks, react-dom, shared layout code, webpack runtime, and main-app — comes to roughly 1.72 MB uncompressed, which I should verify against the real numbers.

I'll settle on roughly 1.7 MB total, skipping further verification of the tiny webpack/main-app chunks since they're negligible. Separately, I'm checking whether react-markdown or remark-gfm are actually imported anywhere in the codebase.

Actually, since it's never imported, webpack won't resolve the module regardless — I can skip verifying this one, it's logically certain. Now checking image-annotation-editor: I need to grep for who imports it, likely CanvasEditor or canvas-node-dialogs, and confirm it's bundled via the page chunk.

For sizing, I want to compare source file sizes to estimate savings from dynamic imports, so I'll list directory contents to get byte counts for CanvasEditor and related components. Separately, I need to verify what loadRegistry returns server-side when hasAnyApiKey checks run — checking nova-models.ts around line 360-380 to see the default registry behavior.

If the server-side registry has no complete models, hasApiKey would be false server-side but true client-side for configured users, causing a disabled attribute mismatch — I want to check whether this affects rendered text or just an attribute by grepping for disabled-conditional rendering in ImageGenerationWorkbench, AgentChatWorkspace, and ReversePromptForm. I'm also tracking a similar potential mismatch in AssetsWorkspace where sort settings loaded from storage could produce a different label server vs client, so I'll check how that label renders too.

Separately, useAgentChat's webSearchEnabled/intentRecognition initializers depend on localStorage availability, which behaves inconsistently across Node versions — this could cause server defaults to diverge from client-stored values, and since intentRecognition seems to toggle structural UI elements like a params bar in AgentChatWorkspace, that's a stronger candidate for a real hydration mismatch than a simple attribute diff.

I want to grep for how intentRecognition and webSearchEnabled conditionally render markup in AgentChatWorkspace, ImageGenerationWorkbench, and ReversePromptForm.

Next I need to check workspace-task-service for how blobUrls get set on completion, since that ties into the revoked blob URL issue, then peek at canvas-thumbnail.tsx for image loading, look at prompt-gallery-data's fetch calls for remote sources, and check window listeners in CanvasEditor and infinite-canvas.

I'm also planning to check agent-context-store's loadAgentSession around its thumbnail handling, plus gif-job-store and reverse-prompt-store's readAsDataURL usages, though given my 15-finding cap and word limit I should prioritize and possibly skip the lower-priority ones. I'll do one more parallel batch of greps across the workspace components to check for disabled states or similar patterns.

j. Grep Workspace.tsx for sort label rendering, then check S3AssetBrowser's grid handling to see if it's virtualizing thumbnails or creating object URLs per item with per-object IPC reads. I'll pull those file sections in parallel to keep things moving.
The main findings are confirmed. I'm running one last batch of checks on API-key and hydration text, blob-URL ownership, canvas listeners and the S3 grid.

payload.text:
I have enough evidence now to write the final report, but let me double-check the hydration issue #418 first: the SSR HTML shows empty state text while the client hydrates with stored jobs and API key state, confirming the mismatch.

There's also a separate structural mismatch with hasApiKey — server returns false from getInitialRegistry when no models have keys, while client returns true if any key is configured, affecting several components with conditional branches. I'm fairly confident this second mismatch happens whenever any API key is configured, independent of stored jobs, which is a distinct issue from the one the user described.

I should also check whether localStorage exists during Node SSR, since the intentRecognition initial state depends on `typeof localStorage !== 'undefined'`, and Node's support for it varies by version, which could cause yet another server/client mismatch.

That would throw ReferenceError and crash the build on the server, so since the build succeeded, localStorage must have been undefined there, meaning server state defaulted to webSearch false and intentRecognition true — but if a user toggled intentRecognition off client-side, the conditional render at line 937 would create a structural mismatch versus the server output.

I want to keep the final answer concise: the primary cause is the jobs count text in JobsHeader, with secondary causes being the hasApiKey structural branch, the intentRecognition toggle, and the assets sort label. I should double check getInitialRegistry and the ImageGenerationWorkbench branch around line 640, along with loadAssetSettings, before finalizing.

Now I'm looking at AssetsWorkspace around line 84, where the window check falls back to default sort and viewSize values used in the state initializer — if a user previously stored 'oldest' as their sort preference, the rendered label text would differ from the server's default, causing another conditional mismatch tied to user preference changes.

I also notice a Suspense reference in the RSC payload, which suggests Next.js is streaming metadata boundaries — I need to figure out where that Suspense boundary actually sits in the tree.

Right, LayoutRouter's chain doesn't wrap in Suspense unconditionally in Next 15. I still can't confirm the exact placement without seeing the full truncated line, so I should grep index.txt for occurrences of that Suspense marker with surrounding context to check its actual position.

Actually, stepping back, the real question is about React's hydration mismatch behavior itself rather than pinning down this exact metadata outlet detail. In React 19, when hydration fails and there's no nearby Suspense boundary, React discards the server-rendered DOM for that root and re-renders the whole tree client-side, surfacing this through onRecoverableError with a message about the tree being regenerated on the client since the root container is essentially the whole document that Next hydrates.

Since it's `<html>`/`<head>`/`<body>` being treated as singletons, React clears and rebuilds their children rather than removing the singleton elements themselves. Practically, that means the entire app re-renders from scratch client-side—every component's initializers run again (state initializers reparsing JSON, registry loads, etc.), doubling that work and wasting the original hydration pass, with any hydration-only elements getting recreated and then cleaned up on the next render.

So the app essentially renders twice on startup, and the static HTML provides no real benefit here. I'm fairly confident this is the cause -- the text mismatch "共 0 条" vs "共 N 条" in JobsHeader matches the "when stored jobs exist" condition exactly, though I should check whether the hasApiKey branch actually comes first in DOM order.

Actually before HistoryJobList, ImageGenerationWorkbench appears earlier in non-wide mode. If the user has API keys configured, that disabled-state conditional would trigger a mismatch first -- but I need to figure out whether that's a text mismatch or an element-type mismatch depending on what each branch renders, since React 19 handles those differently under the same #418 error code.

So the reported "text mismatch" suggests the disabled branch renders the same element type but different text, or that hasApiKey isn't actually mismatched on the server. I should check the actual code around line 640 and confirm what getInitialRegistry reports for hasApiKey, and also verify whether hydration stops at the first mismatch or continues past it.

In non-wide mode, ImageGenerationWorkbench hydrates before HistoryJobList, so if there's a mismatch inside the workbench's disabled logic (like the API key check), that would be the first one encountered, producing this text mismatch error.

But that would fire regardless of stored jobs, just based on whether keys exist. Since the user specifically noted it happens "when stored jobs exist," maybe fresh users without jobs also lack configured keys, which would explain why they never hit this. I need to check the workbench code around the disabled state and also verify how the model registry initializes API keys.

I confirmed there's no Suspense boundary or loading.tsx anywhere in the app, so that's a solid finding I can note carefully. I'm also flagging that saveJobs gets called inside the setState updater for job persistence, which is problematic since updater functions must stay pure — StrictMode double-invocation in dev could cause duplicate writes.

I also see that useWorkspaceJobs' mount effect redundantly reloads and re-saves jobs on every startup, doubling the JSON parse/stringify work, and the failed hydration causes the initializer to run twice. Beyond that, the workspace object is recreated on every render, causing the subscribe/unsubscribe effect and handler callbacks tied to it to fire needlessly on every WorkspaceShell render.

Now I'm tracing how identity churn cascades: handleCheckStatus's dependencies keep changing so it constantly breaks WaitingJobCard's memoization, and an inline cancel handler passed as a prop guarantees that memo never holds. Then when queueStatus updates arrive via WebSocket, the whole shell re-renders, cascading through all seven workspace components—including PromptGallery whose memo is also defeated by an inline handler—down into HistoryJobList, VirtualJobList, and each rendered job card.

Beyond that, inline onRetry/onClear handlers defeat CompletedJobCard's memo on every render, and AgentChatWorkspace's inline onCopy/onDelete/onRollback do the same to every message bubble. On top of the render churn, HistoryJobList's per-second clock tick while a job is active also forces re-renders of every visible card, and AgentChatWorkspace runs its own 1-second interval during generation regardless of which tab is focused.

The streaming markdown render is a real hotspot too — it reparses the entire accumulated text on every animation-frame flush, which is quadratic over a long response, and since the message list isn't virtualized, every bubble re-renders on each frame due to those same inline callbacks. I've confirmed HistoryJobList does virtualize per day group, though each group still renders all its jobs internally, so a day with hundreds of jobs could still blow up performance within a single virtual row.

Also since reload() runs on every tab activation, it likely produces new asset object identities each time, causing each thumbnail's effect to revoke and re-fetch its blob and create a new object URL for every visible thumbnail whenever the user reopens the tab, which means a visible flash plus IDB churn. I'm double-checking whether listAssets actually returns fresh objects on each read from IDB to confirm this.

Turning to the prompt gallery, I notice it isn't virtualized -- it uses an incremental "load more" pattern that grows the DOM unbounded as the user scrolls, since PromptCards stay mounted with observers that aren't cleaned up after becoming visible. More importantly, the imageCache Set is recreated on every image load, so its identity changes and defeats memoization for every mounted PromptCard, triggering a full re-render cascade across the gallery each time a single image loads.

Looking at S3AssetBrowser next, the object list isn't virtualized either, and each S3Thumbnail fetches its thumbnail immediately on mount with no visibility gating, so a folder with a thousand objects fires a thousand simultaneous thumbnail reads and blob URL creations at once. I'm also checking whether load-more's mergeByKey logic properly preserves existing object references or recreates them unnecessarily.

Now I'm checking hidden-tab work — PromptGallery fetches the blacklist and all prompt sources from remote GitHub proxies on mount whenever showPromptGallery mode is active, even before the tab is visible.

I should quickly grep for the fetchAllPromptSources definition to confirm, since it's cheap to check. I'm also noting the scroll listener stays attached even when hidden, and that the filtering logic runs the Chinese regex plus blacklist check across all prompts as the base seed set.

I'm looking at CanvasWorkspace now: CanvasEditor stays mounted once a project opens even after switching tabs, and it keeps window-level keydown/paste listeners active globally, which could cause performance issues or incorrect Delete/paste handling while the canvas is hidden — I still need to check whether those handlers verify focus first.

I'm also flagging that useCanvasStore hydrates all projects (with all nodes) from localforage at startup regardless of active tab, which could be costly if nodes embed data URLs — worth noting as a low-confidence, unverified size concern. CanvasThumbnail seems fine since it just renders placeholder divs, not actual images, for each project node.

Similarly, GifGenerationWorkspace's interval only runs during active generation, but useGifWorkflow may eagerly convert stored gif jobs to data URLs at startup — I'll list this as suspected alongside the reverse-prompt-store, which also seems to convert stored files to data URLs on mount for history loading. Now I'm looking at the chunk dependency structure: startup loads chunks 736, 902, and page, plus framework, main, and a large 4bd1b696 chunk likely tied to react-dom or Next's client runtime. There's also a 222KB chunk (794) that doesn't appear in page or layout deps directly—I suspect it's part of the app-router client runtime loaded via main-app, and I want to verify this by checking index.html for its reference. I also note the polyfills chunk only loads via nomodule for legacy browsers, and there are two small async chunks (899 and 966) that appear to come from a dynamic import related to canvas/node generation.

Adding up all the startup JS chunks—page, the 902 chunk, 736, framework, 4bd1b696, 794, main, webpack, main-app, and layout—I get roughly 2.05MB of raw JS parsed at startup, though I need to double check whether both main and main-app are actually loaded together given this is an app-router build.

I want to verify exactly which chunks index.html actually references, so I'm going to grep for the specific hashed filenames like 794-fa0d3f5a04f3a105.js, main-e74a1f9601ed6754.js, 4bd1b696-e7155c3f1a5fcdfa.js, framework-41d3731de4d1d404.js, and polyfills-42372ed130431b0a.js to confirm they're actually referenced.

For attribution, since 736 is shared between page and layout while 902 is page-only, I suspect 902 holds the vendor libraries specific to this page (jszip, fflate, gifenc, localforage, lucide, base-ui, zustand, nanoid, tanstack virtual) while 737 is the actual app code and 736 has shared UI dependencies like radix/tailwind-merge/clsx.

I'll check each file for distinctive literal strings using Select-String with -SimpleMatch -Quiet. For jszip, I can look for "has been removed in JSZip 3.0" as a unique signature, and for fflate I can search for its characteristic error message strings like "invalid UTF-8 data" or "unexpected EOF".

I'm also identifying "date not in range 1980-2099" as fflate-specific since jszip doesn't have that check, and for gifenc I'm looking at the "NETSCAPE2.0" string used when writing the application extension header.

For localforage, "No available storage method found." is a distinctive literal string I can use, and I'm now trying to find a unique signature string from the canvas editor code, though the "节点式画布生图" text belongs to CanvasWorkspace rather than the editor itself.

Rather than digging deeper into individual strings, I realize attribution can rely on the import graph directly: CanvasWorkspace statically imports CanvasEditor, and WorkspaceShell statically imports CanvasWorkspace, so CanvasEditor and its dependencies are confirmed to be part of the startup bundle. Now I want to check the sizes of these source modules to figure out what could reasonably be split out.

Since the actual bundle chunk sizes matter more than source file sizes, I want to also check if AssetsWorkspace's grid is virtualized — grepping showed no useVirtualizer usage, so I should look closer at how it renders visible assets, possibly through a paginated "visible count" pattern rather than true virtualization.

I still have several code reads queued: examining thumbnail blob URL creation per card in AssetsWorkspace and whether object URLs get properly revoked, checking S3AssetBrowser for eager loading behavior even when hidden, and looking at AgentChatWorkspace's image memoization plus how agent-context-store loads all session images upfront via readAsDataURL during session load.

I also want to check AgentMessageBubble for per-message blob URL creation and inline callbacks breaking memoization, review upload-image-cache.ts for eager data URL loading, inspect ReversePromptForm/reverse-prompt-store for mount-time data URL conversion, and check gif-job-store's readAsDataURL usage during job loading. CanvasEditor itself seems to only mount conditionally when a project is active, so it may not be an eager-load culprit initially.

Now I'm suspecting the workspace list's CanvasThumbnail component might render node images for every project even when kept mounted but hidden — worth checking canvas-thumbnail.tsx. I also want to verify whether the canvas store hydrates its entire persisted state via localforage at module load time regardless of whether the canvas tab is ever opened, and whether node objects still carry inline dataUrl images despite the storageKey approach existing. I should also check what happens to CanvasEditor after it's mounted once and the user switches tabs — does keepMounted retain the full image-heavy state in memory afterward?

Beyond that, I want to trace whether CanvasEditor keeps its ResizeObserver, animation loops, and interval timers running while its tab is hidden, and check for any window-level keydown listeners that could keep firing (e.g. a Delete shortcut deleting nodes) even when the user's focus is elsewhere. I also plan to look at WorkspaceHeader's animation loop, the image generation workbench's upload cache loading behavior, the toast component's timer handling, and whether SettingsModal does any work while closed or only early-returns when not open.

I'm also flagging server/client hydration mismatches: hasAnyApiKey and related registry loading return different defaults on server vs client, which could cause disabled states and button text (like the "please configure API key" prompt) to differ between renders, so I want to grep for those conditional disabled/text patterns. Similarly, useAgentChat's webSearchEnabled and intentRecognition initializers depend on localStorage availability checks that might behave differently across Node versions, which is another potential hydration mismatch source.

So server defaults apply while client reflects actual stored values, meaning if the user toggled web search on, the composer UI would show a different state on hydration — causing a mismatch, though a class-only change wouldn't trigger a full DOM error, just a style difference.

I'm now trying to recall whether attribute mismatches like this even surface as warnings in production builds. React's hydration diffing for attributes typically only runs in development, while production builds mainly check for unmatched text content, so this kind of mismatch might not throw the specific error I'm chasing at all.

It continues checking that text content matches for hydration, comparing the DOM element's actual text against expected children unless warnings are suppressed, then returns whether hydration succeeded—if it fails, `prepareToHydrateHostInstance` throws a hydration mismatch error.

That matches: 418("text") for text mismatches, 418("HTML") for structural mismatches, and attribute mismatches only warn in DEV. The thrown HydrationMismatchException propagates through the work loop, and if no Suspense boundary catches it, the root falls back to full client rendering instead of using the server markup.

Once the root is flagged for client render, the existing DOM is cleared and rebuilt, and Next.js's default onRecoverableError surfaces the minified 418 error via console/reportError, matching the described symptom of the mismatch firing on every load. The likely culprit is a counter or count string like "共 0 条" differing between server and client render.

Since the paragraph contains multiple JSX text children rather than one interpolated string, each becomes a separate HostText fiber, and hydration compares each node's actual DOM value against the expected text -- any mismatch there triggers the same unmatched-text hydration error path.

If hydration fails and the safety flag is on, React throws a hydration mismatch error. Since checkForUnmatchedText normalizes whitespace but "0" differs from "5", that text mismatch triggers the 418 error — confirmed by the SSR HTML showing "共 0 条" and "暂无日期" while the client state comes from the useState initializer in useWorkspaceJobs.ts at line 31.

Now I'm tracing which mismatch React actually hits first in tree order — loadJobs returns an empty array on the server due to the window guard, but on the client it returns stored jobs. There's also a DayIndex mismatch: server renders a bare trigger button since groups is empty, while client wraps it in a Popover with extra Radix attributes, plus a text difference between "暂无日期" and "今天". But since React hydrates in document order and the image-generation tab renders before the agent tab, the JobsHeader's "共 {jobsList.length} 条" text is likely the very first mismatch encountered — though I need to check what's rendered even earlier in the image-generation panel.

I'm now considering ImageGenerationWorkbench, which passes `disabled={!workspace.hasApiKey}`. Since server-side loadRegistry falls back to a default registry with no complete models, hasApiKey resolves to false there, while on the client with configured keys it resolves to true — so if the component conditionally renders something like a "配置 API 密钥" button based on `disabled`, that's another structural mismatch that would trigger for essentially any real user. I want to grep across ImageGenerationWorkbench, AgentChatWorkspace, and ReversePromptForm for conditional rendering tied to `disabled` or `hasApiKey` to confirm this.

Other things look fine — wideMode, mounted/desktopRuntime, and useQueueStatus are consistent between server and client. But AssetsWorkspace's SSR fallback for sort/viewSize preferences could cause a text mismatch if it's used inside a useState initializer, so I need to check how that's wired up. Similarly, I suspect usePromptGalleryConfig's mode setting, if read from storage during initialization, could cause showPromptGallery to differ between server and client, creating a structural mismatch in the tab rendering — worth checking that hook next, along with running a broader grep across all these suspects.

I'm planning several checks: scanning ImageGenerationWorkbench, AgentChatWorkspace, ReversePromptForm, and GifGenerationWorkspace for disabled-state text conditionals, reading through usePromptGalleryConfig.ts and AssetsWorkspace, and searching index.html and the JS chunks for various signature strings and chunk hashes to pin down which bundle is stale. Two more suspects stand out: the SSR/client mismatch in loadAssetSettings's sort/viewSize defaults could cause a text mismatch on hydration, and the AssetsWorkspace grid's non-virtualized incremental loading means every thumbnail creates its own IntersectionObserver and blob URL, which gets revoked and recreated on every reload since the asset objects get new identities each time listAssets runs.

Confirmed the tab-switch churn issue: reloading on active causes all visible thumbnails to re-fetch blobs from IndexedDB and recreate object URLs, causing a visible flash — medium severity. There's also a minor issue where the preview resets whenever visibleAssets changes.

Now I want to check agent-context-store's loadAgentSession, particularly whether images are kept as data URLs in state via readAsDataURL, and look at AgentChatWorkspace where inline closures for copy/delete/rollback are defeating the memoized message bubble, plus how streaming text updates trigger full re-renders on every animation frame.

The streaming re-render issue is real: every AgentChatWorkspace update during generation forces all bubbles to reconcile (memo defeated) and runs markdown parsing on the full accumulated streaming text each frame, even though each bubble's own markdown is memoized by its own text. There's also a one-second interval that re-renders the entire workspace including all bubbles during generation, and this keeps running even when the Agent tab is hidden since it's only gated by phase, not visibility.

The GifGenerationWorkspace has a similar interval gated only by workflow status, but its impact is low since it only runs during generation. I'm now checking whether the canvas-node intervals behave similarly.

I'm now checking whether CanvasEditor stays mounted after tab switches and whether it still handles keyboard events while hidden -- this could be both a performance and correctness issue, since a hidden canvas shouldn't be intercepting keystrokes. I want to grep for its keydown listener to confirm.

I'm also skimming a few smaller pieces: the WorkspaceHeader animation frame looks benign (likely an image viewer), the image generation workbench's settings-reading effect looks fine, and the toast component appears to manage its own timer correctly. Now I'm checking how the canvas store hydrates from persisted storage on load.

I have enough evidence now to write the final report, but let me double-check the hydration issue #418 first: the SSR HTML shows empty state text while the client hydrates with stored jobs and API key state, confirming the mismatch.

There's also a separate structural mismatch with hasApiKey — server returns false from getInitialRegistry when no models have keys, while client returns true if any key is configured, affecting several components with conditional branches. I'm fairly confident this second mismatch happens whenever any API key is configured, independent of stored jobs, which is a distinct issue from the one the user described.

I should also check whether localStorage exists during Node SSR, since the intentRecognition initial state depends on `typeof localStorage !== 'undefined'`, and Node's support for it varies by version, which could cause yet another server/client mismatch.

That would throw ReferenceError and crash the build on the server, so since the build succeeded, localStorage must have been undefined there, meaning server state defaulted to webSearch false and intentRecognition true — but if a user toggled intentRecognition off client-side, the conditional render at line 937 would create a structural mismatch versus the server output.

I want to keep the final answer concise: the primary cause is the jobs count text in JobsHeader, with secondary causes being the hasApiKey structural branch, the intentRecognition toggle, and the assets sort label. I should double check getInitialRegistry and the ImageGenerationWorkbench branch around line 640, along with loadAssetSettings, before finalizing.

Now I'm looking at AssetsWorkspace around line 84, where the window check falls back to default sort and viewSize values used in the state initializer — if a user previously stored 'oldest' as their sort preference, the rendered label text would differ from the server's default, causing another conditional mismatch tied to user preference changes.

I also notice a Suspense reference in the RSC payload, which suggests Next.js is streaming metadata boundaries — I need to figure out where that Suspense boundary actually sits in the tree.

Right, LayoutRouter's chain doesn't wrap in Suspense unconditionally in Next 15. I still can't confirm the exact placement without seeing the full truncated line, so I should grep index.txt for occurrences of that Suspense marker with surrounding context to check its actual position.

Actually, stepping back, the real question is about React's hydration mismatch behavior itself rather than pinning down this exact metadata outlet detail. In React 19, when hydration fails and there's no nearby Suspense boundary, React discards the server-rendered DOM for that root and re-renders the whole tree client-side, surfacing this through onRecoverableError with a message about the tree being regenerated on the client since the root container is essentially the whole document that Next hydrates.

Since it's `<html>`/`<head>`/`<body>` being treated as singletons, React clears and rebuilds their children rather than removing the singleton elements themselves. Practically, that means the entire app re-renders from scratch client-side—every component's initializers run again (state initializers reparsing JSON, registry loads, etc.), doubling that work and wasting the original hydration pass, with any hydration-only elements getting recreated and then cleaned up on the next render.

So the app essentially renders twice on startup, and the static HTML provides no real benefit here. I'm fairly confident this is the cause -- the text mismatch "共 0 条" vs "共 N 条" in JobsHeader matches the "when stored jobs exist" condition exactly, though I should check whether the hasApiKey branch actually comes first in DOM order.

Actually before HistoryJobList, ImageGenerationWorkbench appears earlier in non-wide mode. If the user has API keys configured, that disabled-state conditional would trigger a mismatch first -- but I need to figure out whether that's a text mismatch or an element-type mismatch depending on what each branch renders, since React 19 handles those differently under the same #418 error code.

So the reported "text mismatch" suggests the disabled branch renders the same element type but different text, or that hasApiKey isn't actually mismatched on the server. I should check the actual code around line 640 and confirm what getInitialRegistry reports for hasApiKey, and also verify whether hydration stops at the first mismatch or continues past it.

In non-wide mode, ImageGenerationWorkbench hydrates before HistoryJobList, so if there's a mismatch inside the workbench's disabled logic (like the API key check), that would be the first one encountered, producing this text mismatch error.

But that would fire regardless of stored jobs, just based on whether keys exist. Since the user specifically noted it happens "when stored jobs exist," maybe fresh users without jobs also lack configured keys, which would explain why they never hit this. I need to check the workbench code around the disabled state and also verify how the model registry initializes API keys.

I confirmed there's no Suspense boundary or loading.tsx anywhere in the app, so that's a solid finding I can note carefully. I'm also flagging that saveJobs gets called inside the setState updater for job persistence, which is problematic since updater functions must stay pure — StrictMode double-invocation in dev could cause duplicate writes.

I also see that useWorkspaceJobs' mount effect redundantly reloads and re-saves jobs on every startup, doubling the JSON parse/stringify work, and the failed hydration causes the initializer to run twice. Beyond that, the workspace object is recreated on every render, causing the subscribe/unsubscribe effect and handler callbacks tied to it to fire needlessly on every WorkspaceShell render.

Now I'm tracing how identity churn cascades: handleCheckStatus's dependencies keep changing so it constantly breaks WaitingJobCard's memoization, and an inline cancel handler passed as a prop guarantees that memo never holds. Then when queueStatus updates arrive via WebSocket, the whole shell re-renders, cascading through all seven workspace components—including PromptGallery whose memo is also defeated by an inline handler—down into HistoryJobList, VirtualJobList, and each rendered job card.

Beyond that, inline onRetry/onClear handlers defeat CompletedJobCard's memo on every render, and AgentChatWorkspace's inline onCopy/onDelete/onRollback do the same to every message bubble. On top of the render churn, HistoryJobList's per-second clock tick while a job is active also forces re-renders of every visible card, and AgentChatWorkspace runs its own 1-second interval during generation regardless of which tab is focused.

The streaming markdown render is a real hotspot too — it reparses the entire accumulated text on every animation-frame flush, which is quadratic over a long response, and since the message list isn't virtualized, every bubble re-renders on each frame due to those same inline callbacks. I've confirmed HistoryJobList does virtualize per day group, though each group still renders all its jobs internally, so a day with hundreds of jobs could still blow up performance within a single virtual row.

Also since reload() runs on every tab activation, it likely produces new asset object identities each time, causing each thumbnail's effect to revoke and re-fetch its blob and create a new object URL for every visible thumbnail whenever the user reopens the tab, which means a visible flash plus IDB churn. I'm double-checking whether listAssets actually returns fresh objects on each read from IDB to confirm this.

Turning to the prompt gallery, I notice it isn't virtualized -- it uses an incremental "load more" pattern that grows the DOM unbounded as the user scrolls, since PromptCards stay mounted with observers that aren't cleaned up after becoming visible. More importantly, the imageCache Set is recreated on every image load, so its identity changes and defeats memoization for every mounted PromptCard, triggering a full re-render cascade across the gallery each time a single image loads.

Looking at S3AssetBrowser next, the object list isn't virtualized either, and each S3Thumbnail fetches its thumbnail immediately on mount with no visibility gating, so a folder with a thousand objects fires a thousand simultaneous thumbnail reads and blob URL creations at once. I'm also checking whether load-more's mergeByKey logic properly preserves existing object references or recreates them unnecessarily.

Now I'm checking hidden-tab work — PromptGallery fetches the blacklist and all prompt sources from remote GitHub proxies on mount whenever showPromptGallery mode is active, even before the tab is visible.

I should quickly grep for the fetchAllPromptSources definition to confirm, since it's cheap to check. I'm also noting the scroll listener stays attached even when hidden, and that the filtering logic runs the Chinese regex plus blacklist check across all prompts as the base seed set.

I'm looking at CanvasWorkspace now: CanvasEditor stays mounted once a project opens even after switching tabs, and it keeps window-level keydown/paste listeners active globally, which could cause performance issues or incorrect Delete/paste handling while the canvas is hidden — I still need to check whether those handlers verify focus first.

I'm also flagging that useCanvasStore hydrates all projects (with all nodes) from localforage at startup regardless of active tab, which could be costly if nodes embed data URLs — worth noting as a low-confidence, unverified size concern. CanvasThumbnail seems fine since it just renders placeholder divs, not actual images, for each project node.

Similarly, GifGenerationWorkspace's interval only runs during active generation, but useGifWorkflow may eagerly convert stored gif jobs to data URLs at startup — I'll list this as suspected alongside the reverse-prompt-store, which also seems to convert stored files to data URLs on mount for history loading. Agent's session loading at mount is fine since it's the default tab, though its 1s generation interval keeps running even when hidden, which is worth flagging.

The bigger issue I've verified is in useServerTaskPolling: every socket 'processing' message triggers replaceJob unconditionally, creating a new jobs array even when status hasn't changed, causing a full saveJobs persist and cascading re-renders through WorkspaceShell — the fix is to bail out early when nothing actually changed.

On memory, loadStoredImages pulls every IndexedDB record at startup including full base64 reference images, and all of that gets pushed into React state for every job regardless of whether it's needed.

Desktop compounds this further by reading each reference file over IPC and re-encoding it via FileReader, inflating size by roughly a third and stacking N IPC calls at startup, all retained as JS strings in memory. There's also a suspicion that legacy IDB records store raw base64 in the images field itself, meaning old jobs could be loading entire images into state on boot — worth confirming against actual data age. The fix path: load only lightweight job metadata at startup, defer refImages loading until actually needed (preview, retry, canvas import), and switch storage to Blobs with a cursor-based or split-store approach instead of eager full materialization.

Now I'm second-guessing the blobUrls revoke logic — CompletedJobCard revokes job.blobUrls on unmount, but I don't see where workspace-task-service actually assigns blobUrls to the job object; my grep for that field only hit unrelated lines. If nothing ever sets job.blobUrls, the revoke effect is dead code and the stale-URL race I flagged might not actually happen, so I need to search the whole codebase for any assignment to that field before trusting this finding.

Tracing resolveImageAt further: it checks if an image is an IDB reference, resolves it into a blob URL, and caches that URL back into the images array so subsequent calls return the cached blob instead of creating a new one — meaning repeated calls after the first resolve should be safe, aside from a possible race if openPreview fires again before the state update from setImages has landed, which could momentarily create duplicate blob URLs.

Now I want to trace where downloadAndStoreImages' blob URLs actually get consumed downstream, since I saw references to imageReferences and persistedImages elsewhere in workspace-task-service — I need to grep for where downloadAndStoreImages's results are used.

If those blob URLs end up stored in job.images without ever being assigned to job.blobUrls, removeJob's revocation would miss them entirely, meaning each completed job's generated images (potentially large PNGs) would leak for the session's lifetime. That's worth confirming with a targeted grep before flagging it.

Separately, I'm looking at the upload-image-cache module — it stores full data URLs in IndexedDB, reads entire files as data URLs, and hashes the whole array buffer, all of which cause base64 inflation and main-thread decoding for large files. I checked the whole file and there's no eviction logic at all, so the cache grows unbounded in storage, though this is more of a storage concern than a runtime memory leak.

I also noticed saveJobs performs a synchronous JSON.stringify plus a synchronous localStorage/config-set call inside every setState updater for job changes, which I've verified in the code.

Now I'm examining the bundle size breakdown, with the app page chunk at over 737KB (all workspace code loaded upfront) and a vendor chunk over 408KB containing dependencies like gifenc.

I'm also noting other large chunks -- an unattributed shared runtime chunk around 222KB, one likely to be react-dom near 200KB, and a framework chunk that doesn't seem to be referenced by the index.html, suggesting it may belong to an unused pages-router setup.

Continuing down the list: main-e74a1f9601ed6754.js also looks like unloaded pages-router runtime, a shared chunk used by both layout and page, a polyfills bundle only for legacy browsers, and small layout-specific files rounding out the top ten.

Adding up only the chunks I've confirmed are actually referenced in the startup path — page, 902, 794, 4bd1b696, 736, and layout — I'm getting roughly 1.71 MB uncompressed, which I'll note excludes webpack/main-app runtime files I haven't individually verified as referenced.

I'm double-checking that chunk 736 shows up in the layout/page listing, confirming it's loaded, and that 4bd1b696 is genuinely referenced by index.html. Now I'm tracing which heavier modules — the canvas editor components, gif encoder, and backup utilities with fflate/localforage — are candidates for lazy-loading rather than being pulled into the initial bundle.

For jszip, it's imported by AssetsWorkspace and AgentImageGallery, and since Agent is the default tab it currently loads at startup unless I defer it into the click handlers with a dynamic import. I also confirmed react-markdown/remark-gfm aren't actually imported anywhere except a stray comment, so they're dead dependencies I should remove from package.json. My fix is to wrap CanvasWorkspace in a dynamic import with ssr disabled and a loading state.

I should also lazy-mount other heavy panels (assets, prompt gallery, reverse prompt) only on first activation while keeping them mounted afterward, and move jszip/gifenc/fflate imports inside export handlers rather than top-level. But I need to be careful—just using keepMounted with dynamic() still triggers loading at startup since they're rendered, so the real fix requires combining first-activation lazy mount with next/dynamic together. I also need to flag that CanvasEditor isn't mounted at startup but its code still ships in the startup bundle, and once opened it stays mounted.

Beyond that, there are several things left to verify: where blobUrls get set and how downloadAndStoreImages is used, the disabled branch logic in ImageGenerationWorkbench, whether the initial model registry actually excludes API keys, how fetchAllPromptSources fetches its targets, and who imports backup-utils.

Given the tight word budget, I need to keep each finding terse — title, impact, evidence, fix, and verification status, aiming for roughly a dozen findings with a compact table for the top chunks rather than expanding on every detail.
Most findings are confirmed. One last batch checks blob-URL ownership, the API-key hydration branch, the gallery fetch target and the canvas key handler.

In there it caches the fiber node and compares the text node's value against the expected text, checking for suppressed hydration warnings or unmatched text. If there's a mismatch, that's what triggers throwOnHydrationMismatch with a "text" flag.

For elements, tryToClaimNextHydratableInstance checks if it's currently hydrating, validates the hydratable instance against the host context, and attempts to hydrate the next instance -- if that fails, it warns about the non-hydrated instance and throws the mismatch error.
